title: Learning Fine-Grained Bimanual Manipulation with Low-Cost Hardware
abstract: Introduces Action Chunking with Transformers (ACT) and the ALOHA hardware system for fine-grained bimanual manipulation from 50 human demonstrations.

title: Diffusion Policy: Visuomotor Policy Learning via Action Diffusion
abstract: Represents robot visuomotor policies as conditional denoising diffusion processes, achieving state-of-the-art performance across 12 tasks in simulation and 4 tasks in the real world.

title: Octo: An Open-Source Generalist Robot Policy
abstract: Open-source 93M-parameter generalist robot policy trained on 800k episodes from Open X-Embodiment. Supports language and goal-image conditioning across 22 robot embodiments.

title: pi0: A Vision-Language-Action Flow Model for General Robot Control
abstract: Vision-language-action model using flow matching on a pre-trained PaLI-Gemma backbone. Achieves state-of-the-art on dexterous tasks including laundry folding and table busing.

title: RT-1: Robotics Transformer for Real-World Control at Scale
abstract: Transformer-based policy trained on 130k real-world episodes from 13 robots. Achieves 97% success on seen tasks and 76% on unseen instructions via emergent generalization.

title: RT-2: Vision-Language-Action Models Transfer Web Knowledge to Robotic Control
abstract: Co-fine-tunes a PaLM-E vision-language model to directly output robot actions as text tokens, transferring web-scale knowledge to robotic control with emergent capabilities.

title: Mobile ALOHA: Learning Bimanual Mobile Manipulation with Low-Cost Whole-Body Teleoperation
abstract: Extends ALOHA to a mobile base and introduces co-training with static ALOHA data. Achieves complex kitchen tasks (sauteing, wiping) from just 50 task-specific demonstrations.

title: Walk These Ways: Tuning Robot Control for Generalization with Multiplicity of Behavior
abstract: Trains a single locomotion policy with a multiplicative gait parameter space that covers walking, trotting, bounding, and pronking, enabling diverse behaviors from one model.

title: Extreme Parkour with Legged Robots
abstract: Teacher-student distillation pipeline with privileged terrain information enables climbing, gap jumping, and leaping onto 60cm platforms on a quadruped robot.

title: robomimic: A Framework for Robot Learning from Demonstration
abstract: Provides a standardized framework with 5 manipulation tasks and proficiency-stratified human demos for systematic evaluation of imitation learning algorithms.

title: Open X-Embodiment: Robotic Learning Datasets and RT-X Models
abstract: Largest open robotics dataset: 1M+ episodes from 22 embodiments across 21 institutions. Demonstrates positive transfer when co-training across embodiments.

title: LeRobot: Making AI for Robotics More Accessible
abstract: Open-source framework unifying robot policy training, evaluation, and dataset management. Supports ACT, Diffusion Policy, and TD-MPC with standardized data formats.

title: DROID: A Large-Scale In-the-Wild Robot Manipulation Dataset
abstract: 76k demonstrations across 564 scenes and 86 tasks collected on Franka arms across multiple institutions, providing unprecedented scene and task diversity.

title: Learning Agile Locomotion via Adversarial Training
abstract: Uses adversarial terrain and perturbation generators during training to produce robust locomotion policies that transfer reliably to real quadrupeds.

title: UMI on Legs: Making Manipulation Policies Mobile with Manipulation-Centric Whole-body Controllers
abstract: Decouples manipulation policy from locomotion by using a manipulation-centric whole-body controller, enabling existing tabletop policies to work on legged robots.
